facts: The heart has four chambers: two atria on top and two ventricles below.
The right side pumps oxygen-poor blood to the lungs; the left side pumps oxygen-rich blood to the body.
Valves stop blood flowing backwards; their closing makes the lub-dub sound.
Each beat starts at the SA node, the natural pacemaker.
The left ventricle has the thickest wall because it pumps blood to the whole body.

scenes.heading: How does the human heart work?
scenes.subtitle: A pump with four rooms

narration.text: Your heart is a muscle that pumps blood around your whole body.
The heart has four chambers.
The right atrium collects blood returning from the body.
The right ventricle pumps it to the lungs.
The left atrium receives fresh blood from the lungs.
The left ventricle pumps it out to the whole body.
Blood low in oxygen returns from the body.
The right side pumps it to the lungs.
In the lungs, blood picks up oxygen and drops carbon dioxide.
The left side pumps oxygen-rich blood back to the body.

scenes.heading: Step 3: Valves keep blood moving one way

narration.text: First, an atrium squeezes and pushes blood down.
A valve opens to let blood into the ventricle.
When the ventricle squeezes, the valve shuts so blood cannot flow back.
The lub-dub sound of a heartbeat is the valves closing.

scenes.heading: Step 4: One heartbeat, step by step

events.label: SA node
events.text: The natural pacemaker fires an electrical signal

events.label: Atria
events.text: Atria contract and fill the ventricles

events.label: AV node
events.text: The signal pauses briefly, then passes down

events.label: Ventricles
events.text: Ventricles contract: blood to lungs and body

events.label: Relax
events.text: The muscle relaxes and the chambers refill

narration.text: Each beat starts at the SA node, the heart's natural pacemaker.
The AV node delays the signal so the atria finish emptying.
Then the ventricles contract and push blood out.
Finally the muscle relaxes and the chambers refill.
When you run or play, your muscles work harder.
Working muscles need more oxygen and glucose.
So the heart beats faster and pumps more blood each minute.
A resting adult heart usually beats about sixty to one hundred times a minute.
Faster blood flow brings the muscles the oxygen they need.

scenes.heading: Quick check
scenes.question: Which chamber pumps blood to the whole body?

narration.text: Quick check. Which chamber pumps blood to the body?
The left ventricle. It has the thickest, strongest wall.
Quick check. What is the job of the valves?
They stop blood from flowing backwards.
Quick check. What starts each heartbeat?
The SA node, the heart's built-in pacemaker.
